name: Build Under Constraints
description: First-person, point-of-view creator content where ONE on-screen character walks the viewer through an aspirational, actionable plan — 'If I had $1000 today, here's exactly what I'd do', day-in-the-life, side-hustle challenges. Aspirational, candid, energetic, concrete. Pairs best with the Continuity format (character-locked img2img) where the same person carries every scene. Layer it when the channel is creator-led advice / money / productivity / challenge content.
audience: Viewers who want a relatable, first-person walkthrough they can imagine themselves doing — aspirational money / productivity / self-improvement audiences.
perspective_policy: Second-person practical simulation, never a hype monologue.

narrative_quality_contract.opening_policy: Start with the constraint, resource limit, or decision the viewer must work through.
narrative_quality_contract.closing_policy: End with the most useful decision rule.

narrative_rules: Opening beat premise_setup: set the premise in one line — the constraint, the amount, the deadline.
Opening beat personal_check_in: say where you are standing and what you are holding as you start; keep it physical.
Opening beat what_youll_learn: promise specifics — the actual steps, not the mindset.
Opening beat not_advice_note: one line that this is what you would do, not advice for anybody else’s situation.
Opening beat subscribe_cta: one line at the end of the opening, never at the start.
Opening beat transition: stop talking about it and start doing it.
title_rules: Titles are FIRST-PERSON and pay off a concrete premise.
Established shapes (vary the constraint/goal across the batch):
- 'If I had {Constraint} today, here's how I'd {Goal}'  (e.g. 'If I had $1000 today, here's how I'd multiply it')
- 'How I'd {Goal} from {Starting Point}'                (e.g. 'How I'd get my first 1000 subscribers from scratch')
- '{Goal}, step by step'                                (e.g. 'Turning $100 into real income, step by step')
REQUIRED: name a concrete constraint or starting point ($1000, a MacBook, 24 hours, zero) and imply a clear result the viewer wants.
FORBIDDEN: vague self-help phrasing ('Unlock your potential'), get-rich-quick hype, all-caps.

pacing_arc: Hook: state the first-person premise ('If I had X today…').
Setup: the starting situation, shown as an establishing scene.
Core: the step-by-step plan, each step its own concrete, visualizable beat.
Momentum: a busier stretch of quick actions (faster cuts).
Payoff: the result, tied back to the opening premise, with a clear call to action.
additional_rules: Anchor each beat to a concrete, visualizable action or location — the planner turns these into scenes.
Prefer short, punchy sentences over long abstract ones; busy passages should imply faster cuts.
Keep one consistent on-screen persona — don't introduce new unnamed people the chain can't render consistently.
Stay aspirational and practical, never preachy or salesy. Show the steps, don't lecture.
Close with a clear payoff or call to action that lands the POV premise.

example_topics: If I had $1000 today, here's exactly what I'd do to multiply it
If I had a MacBook today, here's how I'd make money with it
Starting a side hustle from zero in 24 hours
How I'd get my first 1000 subscribers from scratch
If I lost everything, here's my first 7 days
Turning $100 into a real income, step by step
My exact morning routine to get more done before 9am
How I'd learn a high-income skill in 30 days
audience_hint: Viewers who want a relatable, first-person walkthrough they can imagine themselves doing — aspirational money / productivity / self-improvement audiences.
evidence_expectations: Label hypothetical numbers and outcomes instead of presenting them as guarantees.
Make costs, time, tools, and constraints concrete enough to check.
Separate a personal walkthrough from financial, legal, or professional advice.
idea_system_prompt_role: You generate first-person, point-of-view episode ideas for a creator-led channel where ONE consistent on-screen character carries the whole video. Frame every idea from the creator's perspective and make it lend itself to a sequence of concrete, visualizable moments the character physically moves through (sitting at a desk, opening a laptop, walking into a shop, counting cash). Favour aspirational, actionable, 'here's exactly what I'd do' angles over abstract commentary.
idea_guidance_text: Each idea should imply a clear sequence of scenes the character physically moves through, so the continuity chain has distinct beats to render. 'How to save money' is too abstract; 'If I had $1000 today, here's exactly what I'd do to multiply it' gives a walkable, scene-by-scene arc. Keep it first-person and concrete.
script_context: Write in first person as one on-screen creator walking the viewer through a concrete plan, step by step. Anchor each beat to a physical, visualizable action or location — the visual planner turns each into its own scene.
script_system_prompt_role: You are writing a first-person, point-of-view narration where ONE creator carries the whole video and the visuals are rendered scene-by-scene to match the audio. Give the visual planner clear, concrete physical beats to latch onto — what the on-screen creator is doing, holding, looking at, or where they are. Short, vivid, action-anchored sentences beat long abstract ones. The tone is aspirational, candid, and practical — 'here's exactly what I'd do'.
script_closing_hint: End on the payoff that resolves the opening 'if I had…' premise, then a clean call to action.

narrator_styles.label: Casual first-person
narrator_styles.description: Relaxed, conversational 'talking to a friend' voice. The default for POV creator content.

narrator_styles.label: High-energy hustle
narrator_styles.description: Faster, punchier, motivational — leans into momentum and quick wins.

narrator_styles.label: Calm and deliberate
narrator_styles.description: Measured, confident, 'let me walk you through this' pacing. Good for thoughtful walkthroughs.
